summary: Group 2 (Approve & Onboard + Onboarding Dashboard + template automations) fully verified. 12/12 pytest cases pass, covering: application_received auto-fire on submit, application_approved auto-fire on PUT /applications/{id}/status=Approved, POST /applications/{id}/approve-onboard happy path (member created at profile_incomplete with approved_at, fully_onboarded_notified=False, application flipped to Converted to Member with decision_history Approved entry, application_approved comm recorded with acting admin as sender, onboarding_profile comm recorded on member), 400 on second call, 400 for inquiry type, /onboarding/pipeline shape+stage_order+labels+counts+all entry fields, role and stage filters (counts reflect role filter, not stage filter), Declined applications excluded, fully_onboarded_welcome one-time trigger + stage=fully_onboarded + no re-fire on retoggle, and Group-1 regression (9+ templates present incl. all 4 automation keys, /comms/preview + /comms/send happy path). UI: /portal/onboarding-board renders all 7 funnel cards with correct testids, role-filter + stage-filter work, funnel-click filters rows (2 profile_incomplete rows shown, matching Group-2 onboarded members), pipeline-row-<id> and remind-<id> present and remind dialog opens with reminder-template-select / reminder-channel / reminder-send. ApplicationDetail: approve-onboard-btn visible for super_admin on ambassador app, click succeeds and navigates to /portal/members/<new-id> with 'Approved & onboarding started' toast; Communications tab of the (now Converted) application shows both Application Received and Application Approved rows.
critical_code_review_comments: Preview upstream email provider is rate-limiting (429) heavily under bursty send patterns; log_and_send retries 3x with 1.5s/3s backoff (~4.5s/send). Background asyncio.create_task fires-and-forgets — if all 3 retries fail the comm is still recorded with status='failed', so functional correctness is preserved, but automated tests need >=15s of wait for the background comm insert to appear when the provider is throttling. Non-blocking, but consider a shorter per-attempt timeout or an internal test-mode short-circuit.
server.py now 3256 lines — increasingly monolithic; split into modules (applications, onboarding, notifications, comms, events).

update_onboarding uses a stale local `m` for the `not m.get('fully_onboarded_notified')` guard — safe today because the same PUT $sets the flag before scheduling the task, but two concurrent PUTs that both flip the last remaining step would each pass the guard (race). Consider a findOneAndUpdate({fully_onboarded_notified: {$ne: True}}) atomic swap before firing the task.

In _do_convert + approve_and_onboard, member is initialized with onboarding_stage='profile_incomplete' but there is no re-computation until GET /onboarding/pipeline touches _member_onboarding_state — that is where the stage gets normalized; direct GET /members/{id} could show a stale onboarding_stage between events. Not currently a bug because pipeline reads/rewrites it, and the fully_onboarded transition is written directly by update_onboarding.

Onboarding pipeline endpoint always writes onboarding_stage/onboarding_stage_since on GET when it drifts from computed state — this is a side-effect inside a read endpoint. Fine for now, but consider a background reconciler.

rca of the issue: Only intermittent flakiness observed: background comm inserts (application_received / application_approved / fully_onboarded_welcome) can take ~10-20s when Emergent email integration is 429-throttled, because log_and_send retries 3x with 1.5s/3s backoff before still inserting a status='failed' communications row. Mitigation applied in tests: sleep 15-20s after triggers before asserting comm rows.
